findings.claim: Content buffers are keyed only by `${runId}:${kind}` and ignore the wire `messageId`, so on the documented current transport (no `*_END` frames) every distinct logical text span in a run — e.g. assistant text, tool call, more assistant text — is merged into a single coalesced durable row instead of one row per logical span.
findings.evidence: `bufferContent` computes `const key = `${runId}:${kind}`` and concatenates `delta` without inspecting `row.payload.messageId`, while the normalizer emits `messageChunk.messageId` and design.md explicitly states "The current backend emits content deltas and run terminal frames but does not emit text/reasoning end frames." The spec scenario in `specs/frontend-local-first-persistence/spec.md` requires "each buffered logical span is persisted once before the terminal event," which is unimplementable with a single buffer per kind per run. The writer tests only cover a single span, so this is untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the buffer by `${runId}:${kind}:${messageId}` (messageId is present on TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT/REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT wire frames), and/or flush the current span when a `TEXT_MESSAGE_START`/`REASONING_START` frame or a different messageId arrives. Add a writer test with two interleaved/sequential messageIds and no END frames asserting two aggregate rows.

findings.claim: An explicit `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` / `REASONING_MESSAGE_END` frame arriving with an empty buffer is silently dropped — `flushBuffer` returns early on `if (!buffered)` and `ingest` then `return`s without persisting the END row — so a zero-delta message span leaves its persisted START frame with no matching END and a hole in the durable event sequence.
findings.evidence: `if (row.type === "TEXT_MESSAGE_END") { await this.flushBuffer(runId, "message", row); return; }` combined with `flushBuffer`'s `if (!buffered) return;` means the boundary frame itself is never passed to `persistRow` when there is nothing buffered. All other accepted rows (including `TEXT_MESSAGE_START`) persist via `persistRow`, so the durable trace is asymmetric for empty spans.
findings.suggested_fix: When the buffer is empty and an explicit boundary frame exists, persist the END frame as a normal row via `persistRow(runId, row)` instead of dropping it, preserving the START/END pairing in the durable record.

findings.claim: `stopStream` fires `void finalizeRunPersistence(persistence, "cancelled")` without awaiting loop termination, so a terminal `RUN_FINISHED` row already in flight in the stream loop can be ingested after the cancelled `finishRun` and overwrite the run status from `cancelled` back to `finished`.
findings.evidence: `stopStream` sets `activeRunPersistence = null`, calls `void finalizeRunPersistence(persistence, "cancelled")`, and only then calls `streamAbortRef?.abort()`; the abort is observed asynchronously inside the async iterator, and any `await runPersistence.ingest(...)` already processing a `RUN_FINISHED` row calls `store.finishRun({ status: "finished", ... })` (run-event-persistence.ts terminal branch), which issues an unconditional `UPDATE run SET status = $2` with no guard against a prior terminal status.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make `finishRun` refuse to transition out of a terminal status (`WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'running'`), or have `stopStream` abort first and let the loop's AbortError path perform the single cancellation finalization.
